newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Dec natgas sets new highs late on cold.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Dec natgas sets new highs late on cold.

text.p: NYMEX December Henry Hub natgas futures continued to set new highs late Tuesday in moderate trade, driven by forecasts for colder weather later this week and next that should keep cash firm at bidweek. At 1350

EST, December surged 19.2 cents to a new high of $3.17 per million British thermal units. January, which also hit a new high of $3.045, was 11.7 cents higher at $3.025. Other deferreds were up by two to 8.8 cents.
"I'm still pretty bullish. The weather is looking good - it's supposed to be cold this weekend and next. The only thing that can turn it around is warm weather," said one trader.
With storage in some regions still low and below-normal weather forecast for most of the rest of the month, few expected a significant selloff ahead of bidweek later this week.

But some technical traders looked for a pullback after a 20 percent rally in four sessions. They pegged December support in the $3.10 area, then at $2.88 and then in the mid-$2.70s. Resistance was seen at the spot continuation settlement of $3.448 from December 21 when the spot month rallied to an all-time intraday high of $3.72.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped about 10 cents Tuesday to the low-$3.00 area. Midwest pipes climbed 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.80s. New York city gate swing gas gained 10 cents or more to the $3.60s.
NYMEX said 35,565 Hub contracts traded at 1325 EST.
NYMEX December Hub natgas expires Thursday, November 21.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas gained nine cents to a new high of $1.705. Deferred months were untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX said four Alberta contracts traded at 1325 EST.
NYMEX December Permian natgas jumped 22 cents to a new high of $2.95. Other months were untraded at 1400 EST. NYMEX said 15 Permian contracts traded at 1325 EST.
On the KCBT, December rallied 16 cents to a new high of $2.93, while deferreds were up by two to 10 cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.2 cents to 24.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
